concept.definition: A Bidirectional Transformer is a neural architecture that processes input tokens by attending to both left and right context simultaneously in every layer, using self-attention without directional masking.
concept.simpleExplanation: Normally, a language model reads text left-to-right, so each word only knows the words before it. A Bidirectional Transformer reads the whole sentence at once — each word can look at all other words on both sides to understand its meaning. This gives a much richer representation, especially for words whose meaning depends on what comes after them.
concept.analogy: Imagine reading a sentence with a missing word. A left-to-right model is like someone who reads only the words before the blank and guesses. A bidirectional model is like someone who reads the entire sentence first, using both what came before and after the blank, then fills it in with much better accuracy.
concept.whyUsedHere: The paper argues that prior models like GPT are unidirectional (left-to-right), which limits their ability to represent context, especially for token-level tasks like question answering. BERT uses bidirectional self-attention via the Masked Language Model objective, where random tokens are hidden and predicted using full context, enabling deep bidirectional representations.
prerequisites: Transformer architecture (self-attention, multi-head attention, positional encoding)
